results.title: How Thanksgiving became a national holiday: 10 milestones
results.content:
Thanksgiving's place on the fourth Thursday of November comes from federal law, not colonial tradition. Congress put the date into law with a joint resolution, which Franklin D. Roosevelt signed on December 26, 1941. From Lincoln's time until then, the date rested on a proclamation each president issued every autumn. In 1939 that arrangement produced a national argument over which Thursday counted. [...] The two rules produce the same date in most years. They split only when November has five Thursdays. That happens when the month starts on a Wednesday or a Thursday. In those years the fourth Thursday lands on November 22 or 23, a full week before the last Thursday.

Under the fourth-Thursday rule, Thanksgiving always falls between November 22 and November 28. The old last-Thursday custom could push it as late as November 30. [...] The Continental Congress recommended that all 13 states set aside Thursday, December 18, 1777, as a day of thanksgiving after the American victory at Saratoga. It is generally described as the first national thanksgiving observance in the U.S.

The call was a one-time recommendation. Congress named a single date and did not create a recurring holiday.

results.content:
Thanksgiving occurs on the fourth Thursday of November every year, according to Old Farmer's Almanac.

In 2026, Thanksgiving falls on Thursday, Nov. 26.

## Why do we celebrate Thanksgiving?

Thanksgiving is celebrated for many reasons, the first being to show thanks to those we love and care about over a special spread of delicious food. [...] Years later, the holiday was celebrated on the third Thursday of November after President Franklin D. Roosevelt changed Thanksgiving from the last Thursday in November to the second-to-last Thursday in 1939, according to NPR. Roosevelt wanted to boost the economy by creating more time to shop before Christmas.

However, some people continued to celebrate it on the fourth Thursday of November even after Roosevelt's change. [...] Harvest-time feasts date back to many historical peoples, including the Egyptians, Greeks, and Romans.

## When did Thanksgiving become a federal holiday?

The first national Thanksgiving in America was actually celebrated in honor of the creation of the United States Constitution in 1789, known as "Day of Publick Thanksgivin."

During the Civil War, President Abraham Lincoln proclaimed Thanksgiving Day for Thursday, November 26, 1863.

results.title: When is Thanksgiving 2026? Why Turkey Day arrives late this year
results.content:
Thanksgiving is always observed on the fourth Thursday of November, meaning it can fall anywhere from Nov. 22 to Nov. 28, according to NBC Chicago. This year, Thanksgiving falls on Nov. 26, making it one of the latest possible dates for the holiday.

The next time Thanksgiving will fall on Nov. 26 will be in 2037.

The earliest possible date for Thanksgiving is Nov. 22. The holiday last fell on that date in 2018 and will do so again in 2029.

## Other holidays in 2026 [...] The day we're talking about is none other than Thanksgiving. Unlike holidays such as Christmas and Valentine's Day, Thanksgiving falls on a different date each year.

Here's what to know about Thanksgiving and why we celebrate it.



## When is Thanksgiving Day 2026?

This year, Thanksgiving takes place on Thursday, Nov. 26. Last year, the holiday was celebrated on Nov. 27, and on Nov. 28 in 2024.

## Why is Thanksgiving on the 4th Thursday of November? [...] President George Washington proclaimed Nov. 26, 1789, a day of public thanksgiving and prayer at the request of Congress, according to History.com. It was the first time Thanksgiving was celebrated under the country's new constitution.

Presidents after Washington also issued Thanksgiving proclamations, though the dates varied. In 1863, President Abraham Lincoln proclaimed the last Thursday of November a national day of thanksgiving, beginning an annual presidential tradition.
